colors.name: cream
colors.role: background — warm cream paper; every botanical exists against it (the light, light-distinct ground vs SAKURA's dark canvas)

colors.name: ink
colors.role: primary text, the giant 피다, and the SVG line-art strokes themselves (12.4:1 on cream — the ink of the drawing pen)

colors.name: botanical
colors.role: accent: wordmark, section numerals, CTA, focus ring, the deepest stem strokes — the only thing that asks for a click (6.9:1)

colors.name: sage
colors.role: decorative: leaf fills, watercolor washes at low alpha, far stem strokes — never functional text (2.4:1 on cream)

colors.name: blush
colors.role: the single bloom accent: the signature flower's petal wash, one blush per page. Decorative only (1.9:1) — never carries meaning

colors.name: bark
colors.role: secondary text — ink at ~68% composited over cream (5.7:1): glosses, captions, scent descriptions

colors.name: wash-green
colors.role: decorative: mid-tone botanical wash between sage and botanical — the peony leaf watercolor

colors.name: wash-blush
colors.role: decorative: the lighter outer edge of the blush bloom wash, always low-alpha

colors.name: gold
colors.role: decorative only: the anther / stamen dots inside the signature flower, and the hairline date folio

colors.name: hairline
colors.role: decorative: paper-fiber rules and borders at full strength; reads as the paper's own grain

fonts.role: Latin display and italic asides — the wordmark, section titles, the perfumer's voice in italics
all Hangul and the Korean-first voice — scent names, the giant 피다, the sign-off; a Korean serif whose strokes match the Cormorant

texture: Watercolor paper, simulated — not an overlay grain but a behavior. A static feTurbulence (fractalNoise, baseFrequency 0.9, seed 7) sits behind the page as a 4% cream-fiber wash so the cream never reads as flat #fff. The blooming ink is a SECOND, animated feTurbulence + feDisplacementMap acting on the watercolor wash shapes: each wash begins displaced (scale ~60, 'still wet') and a rAF loop eases the displacement down to 0 on reveal, so the color blooms outward and then settles — ink finding its edge. The botanical line-art (stems, leaves, petals) is plain SVG strokes with no filter, so the drawn line stays crisp while only the wash beneath it bleeds.

motion.name: ease-bloom
motion.value: cubic-bezier(0.25, 0.8, 0.3, 1) — quick to open, long to settle, like a petal

motion.name: reveal
motion.value: 900ms ease-bloom, translateY(18px) → 0 and clip-path inset(0 0 100% 0) → inset(0), 90ms stagger per observer batch

motion.name: line-draw intro
motion.value: stroke-dashoffset 1 → 0 over 2200ms ease-bloom per stroke, staggered 120ms by stroke order (stem → branches → leaves → buds)

motion.name: line-draw scrub
motion.value: stroke-dashoffset follows lerp(0.12/frame) of scroll progress within the hero span; scrolling back recedes the crown

motion.name: wash settle
motion.value: feDisplacementMap scale 60 → 0 over 1600ms cubic-out on reveal; turbulence baseFrequency/seed never change, only displacement pays per frame

motion.name: bloom-open (pinned)
motion.value: petal scale 0.42 → 1 and rotate -8° → 0° across the pinned scroll span (0–1), one --bloom-open variable drives all petals

motion.name: bloom lerp
motion.value: 0.14 / 60fps-normalized frame toward the pinned-section scroll target — half-life ~5 frames, responsive but not jittery

motion.name: idle drift
motion.value: the hero branch sways rotate ±0.4° at 11s; the bloom anthers bob translateY ±2px at 7s — mutually prime, never loops
